The birth of modern plastics: In 1907, Leo Hendrick Baekeland, a Belgian scientist working in New York, discovered and patented a revolutionary new synthetic material.
现代塑料的诞生: 1907年，在纽约工作的比利时科学家利奥·亨德里克·贝克兰发现了一种突破性的新型合成材料，并为其取得专利。

The birth of modern plastics: His invention, which he named “Bakelite”, was of enormous technological importance, and effectively launched the modern plastics industry.
现代塑料的诞生: 他把这项发明命名为“Bakelite”（电木）。这项发明在技术上意义重大，实际上开启了现代塑料工业。
column6: technological importance|n. 技术上的重要意义
column9: modern plastics industry|n. 现代塑料工业

The birth of modern plastics: The term ‘plastic’ comes from the Greek plassein, meaning ‘to mould’.
现代塑料的诞生: ‘塑料’一词源自希腊语‘plassein’，意为‘塑造’。

The birth of modern plastics: Some plastics are derived from natural sources, some are semi-synthetic (the result of chemical action on a natural substance), and some are entirely synthetic, that is, chemically engineered from the constituents of coal or oil.
现代塑料的诞生: 有些塑料来源于天然资源，有些是半合成的（即通过化学手段对天然物质进行处理而得），另一些则是完全人工合成的，也就是通过化学方法从煤或石油的成分中制造出来的。

The birth of modern plastics: Some are ‘thermoplastic’, which means that, like candlewax, they melt when heated and can then be reshaped.
现代塑料的诞生: 其中一些塑料属于‘热塑性’，意味着它们像蜡烛蜡一样，在受热时会熔化，并可重新塑形。

The birth of modern plastics: Others are thermosetting’: like eggs, they cannot revert to their original viscous state, and their shape is thus fixed for ever.
现代塑料的诞生: 另一些则是热固性的材料：它们就像鸡蛋一样，无法恢复到原来的粘稠状态，因此它们的形状会永远保持下来。

The birth of modern plastics: Bakelite had the distinction of being the first totally synthetic thermosetting plastic.
现代塑料的诞生: 电木的独特地位在于，它是第一种完全合成的热固性塑料。
modern|adj. 现代: had the distinction of|以……而独特

The birth of modern plastics: The history of today’s plastics begins with the discovery of a series of semi-synthetic thermoplastic materials in the mid-nineteenth century.
现代塑料的诞生: 当今塑料技术的历史可以追溯到19世纪中叶，当时人们发现了一种半合成热塑性材料。

The birth of modern plastics: The impetus behind the development of these early plastics was generated by a number of factors - immense technological progress in the domain of chemistry, coupled with wider cultural changes, and the pragmatic need to find acceptable substitutes for dwindling supplies of ‘luxury’ materials such as tortoiseshell and ivory.
现代塑料的诞生: 推动这些早期塑料发展的因素有好几个：化学领域技术突飞猛进，又逢更广泛的文化变革，此外，玳瑁和象牙等“奢侈”材料的供应不断减少，现实也要求人们找到合用的替代品。
column10: acceptable substitutes|n. 合用的替代品
column11: dwindling supplies|n. 不断减少的供应

The birth of modern plastics: Baekeland’s interest in plastics began in 1885 when, as a young chemistry student in Belgium, he embarked on research into phenolic resins, the group of sticky substances produced when phenol (carbolic acid) combines with an aldehyde (a volatile fluid similar to alcohol).
现代塑料的诞生: 贝克兰对塑料的兴趣始于1885年。当时，他是比利时的一名青年化学学生，开始研究酚醛树脂，即苯酚（石炭酸）和醛（一种与醇相似的挥发性液体）结合时生成的一类黏性物质。

The birth of modern plastics: He soon abandoned the subject, however, only returning to it some years later.
现代塑料的诞生: 然而，他很快放弃了这一研究，直到几年后才重新回归。

The birth of modern plastics: By 1905 he was a wealthy New Yorker, having recently made his fortune with the invention of a new photographic paper.
现代塑料的诞生: 到1905年，他已成为一位富有的纽约人，是因他最近通过发明一种新型照相纸而致富。

The birth of modern plastics: While Baekeland had been busily amassing dollars, some advances had been made in the development of plastics.
现代塑料的诞生: 贝克兰忙着积累财富的那段时间，塑料研发取得了一些进展。
column6: development of plastics|n. 塑料的研发

The birth of modern plastics: The years 1899 and 1900 had seen the patenting of the first semi-synthetic thermosetting material that could be manufactured on an industrial scale.
现代塑料的诞生: 1899年和1900年，第一种可实现工业规模生产的半合成热固性材料获得了专利。

The birth of modern plastics: In purely scientific terms, Baekeland’s major contribution to the field is not so much the actual discovery of the material to which he gave his name, but rather the method by which a reaction between phenol and formaldehyde could be controlled, thus making possible its preparation on a commercial basis.
现代塑料的诞生: 单从科学上说，贝克兰对这一领域的主要贡献，与其说是发现了以他命名的那种材料，不如说是找到了一种控制苯酚与甲醛反应的方法，从而使商业化生产成为可能。
birth|n. 诞生: in purely scientific terms|单从科学角度看
column7: gave his name|以自己的名字命名
column13: on a commercial basis|以商业化的方式

The birth of modern plastics: On 13 July 1907, Baekeland took out his famous patent describing this preparation, the essential features of which are still in use today.
现代塑料的诞生: 1907年7月13日，贝克兰为这项制备工艺取得了那项著名的专利。这一工艺的基本做法沿用至今。

The birth of modern plastics: The original patent outlined a three-stage process, in which phenol and formaldehyde (from wood or coal) were initially combined under vacuum inside a large egg-shaped kettle.
现代塑料的诞生: 最初的专利描述了一个三阶段的过程：首先，苯酚和甲醛（来自木材或煤炭）在真空条件下被放入一个大型蛋形容器中混合在一起。

The birth of modern plastics: The result was a resin known as Novalak, which became soluble and malleable when heated.
现代塑料的诞生: 结果是一种名为诺瓦拉克的树脂，加热后会变得可溶且可塑。

The birth of modern plastics: The resin was allowed to cool in shallow trays until it hardened, and then broken up and ground into powder.
现代塑料的诞生: 这种树脂被放置在浅托盘中冷却，直到其硬化为止。之后，将其破碎成粉末状。

The birth of modern plastics: Other substances were then introduced: including fillers, such as woodflour, asbestos or cotton, which increase strength and moisture resistance, catalysts (substances to speed up the reaction between two chemicals without joining to either) and hexa, a compound of ammonia and formaldehyde which supplied the additional formaldehyde necessary to form a thermosetting resin.
现代塑料的诞生: 随后又加入其他物质，包括木粉、石棉或棉花之类可以提高强度、增强防潮性的填料，还有催化剂（能加快两种化学物质之间的反应，但不与其中任何一种结合的物质），以及六亚甲基四胺。这是一种由氨和甲醛生成的化合物，可为形成热固性树脂提供所需的额外甲醛。

The birth of modern plastics: This resin was then left to cool and harden, and ground up a second time.
现代塑料的诞生: 这种树脂随后被冷却并硬化，然后再次研磨。

The birth of modern plastics: The resulting granular powder was raw Bakelite, ready to be made into a vast range of manufactured objects.
现代塑料的诞生: 所得的颗粒状粉末就是电木原料，可以用来制成多种多样的工业制品。
column6: a vast range of|多种多样的

The birth of modern plastics: In the last stage, the heated Bakelite was poured into a hollow mould of the required shape and subjected to extreme heat and pressure, thereby setting its form for life.
现代塑料的诞生: 最后，把加热的电木倒入具有所需形状的中空模具中，再施以高温和高压，使其永久定型。
column10: heat and pressure|n. 高温和压力

The birth of modern plastics: The design of Bakelite objects, everything from earrings to television sets, was governed to a large extent by the technical requirements of the moulding process.
现代塑料的诞生: 从耳环到电视机，各种电木制品的设计在很大程度上取决于模塑成型工艺的技术要求。
column7: to a large extent|在很大程度上
column9: moulding process|n. 模塑成型工艺

The birth of modern plastics: The object could not be designed so that it was locked into the mould and therefore difficult to extract.
现代塑料的诞生: 该物体无法被设计成固定在模具中，因此很难将其取出。

The birth of modern plastics: A common general rule was that objects should taper towards the deepest part of the mould, and if necessary the product was moulded in separate pieces.
现代塑料的诞生: 一个常见的原则是，物体应向模具最深处逐渐变细，必要时产品可被分成多个独立部件来制作。

The birth of modern plastics: Moulds had to be carefully designed so that the molten Bakelite would flow evenly and completely into the mould.
现代塑料的诞生: 模具必须经过精心设计，使熔融的电木均匀地流入模具，填满各个部位。

The birth of modern plastics: Sharp corners proved impractical and were thus avoided, giving rise to the smooth, ‘streamlined’ style popular in the 1930s.
现代塑料的诞生: 事实证明，尖角在制作上行不通，因此设计时便避开了尖角，由此形成了20世纪30年代流行的那种圆滑的“流线型”风格。

The birth of modern plastics: The thickness of the walls of the mould was also crucial: thick walls took longer to cool and harden, a factor which had to be considered by the designer in order to make the most efficient use of machines.
现代塑料的诞生: 模壁的厚度也至关重要：壁越厚，冷却变硬所需的时间越长。设计者若要最大限度地提高机器利用效率，就必须考虑这一因素。
column11: make the most efficient use of|最高效地利用

The birth of modern plastics: Baekeland’s invention, although treated with disdain in its early years, went on to enjoy an unparalleled popularity which lasted throughout the first half of the twentieth century.
现代塑料的诞生: 贝克兰的发明早年受到轻视，后来却风靡一时，盛况空前，整个20世纪上半叶都是如此。

The birth of modern plastics: It became the wonder product of the new world of industrial expansion – ‘the material of a thousand uses’.
现代塑料的诞生: 它成为工业扩张新时代的奇迹产品——‘千用之材’。

The birth of modern plastics: Being both non-porous and heat-resistant, Bakelite kitchen goods were promoted as being germ-free and sterilisable.
现代塑料的诞生: 电木没有孔隙，又能耐热，因此用电木制成的厨具在宣传中号称不带病菌，而且可以灭菌。

The birth of modern plastics: Electrical manufacturers seized on its insulating properties, and consumers everywhere relished its dazzling array of shades, delighted that they were now, at last, no longer restricted to the wood tones and drab browns of the pre-plastic era.
现代塑料的诞生: 电气产品制造商纷纷青睐其优异的绝缘性能，而广大消费者也非常喜欢它丰富多样的颜色选择。他们很高兴，终于可以不再受到塑料时代那种单调的木质色和暗褐色风格的束缚了。

The birth of modern plastics: It then fell from favour again during the 1950s, and was despised and destroyed in vast quantities.
现代塑料的诞生: 它在20世纪50年代再次失宠，被轻视并被大量毁坏。

The birth of modern plastics: Recently, however, it has been experiencing something of a renaissance, with renewed demand for original Bakelite objects in the collectors’ marketplace, and museums, societies and dedicated individuals once again appreciating the style and originality of this innovative material.
现代塑料的诞生: 不过，近来电木似乎又有些复兴：收藏市场对早期电木原件的需求回升，博物馆、相关团体和热心人士也再次欣赏起这种创新材料的风格与独创性。

modern|adj. 现代: renewed demand|n. 重新增长的需求
